verdict.rationale: Only community evidence covers this story. A 2012 Hacker News comment says Bitbucket switched its markup from Creole to Markdown, with preview in issue comments and a rendered README on the overview page. Another comment describes the README rendering headings and <pre> blocks, so formatted prose is implied, but there are no first-party docs and nothing about syntax-highlighted code. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of Markdown support across READMEs, issues and comments; evidence of syntax highlighting in code blocks; current (not 2012-era) corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can write READMEs, issues, and comments in Markdown that render with formatted prose and highlighted code

citations.quote: Switching markup from Creole to Markdown is very good news, and the preview is back in issue comments
the readme is now narrow and can't expand, so <pre> text is too wide and shows scrollbars
